sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: page gives Province Madang, ISO sra, Ethnologue link, and navigation links 'Saruga in the SIL-PNG Archives' / 'Saruga Publications Available Online' with no resource listed inline; combined with the empty OLAC harvest, no SIL survey report, data paper, wordlist or orthography statement exists for Saruga.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (Index of languages)
sources.note: Index entry cites only Wurm & Hattori 1981 (Language Atlas of the Pacific Area) and Z'graggen 1975 - no descriptive or phonological work as of 1996.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Mabuso languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-32. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-D32 (Saruga = C15)
sources.note: Nothing. Intro sec. 6 (p. viii) 'The transcription is semi-phonemic'; lists Saruga fluctuations (s~h, z~y, y~d, d~r, l~r, w~v~b, p. ix). Wordlist forms carry vowel length but no stress marks (visual check of printed p. 2, saved).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU. vi+154 pp. + map. DOI 10.15144/PL-B41
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: Introduction p.2 'No linguistic material will be presented to justify the classification so as not to overload this book'; Saruga appears only in the classification list (p.21), speaker-rank table, village index and supplementary area list.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38. DOI 10.15144/PL-C38.569
sources.note: Nothing on Saruga; classification, population (C15 Saruga 132) and short comparative lists. Its only prosodic remarks ('appears to be tonal', pp. 585-6) concern Biyom and Isabi, not Saruga.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C19 (Saruga = language 12 'Sr')
sources.note: Survey-wide only, sec. 1.3.3 p. 7: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Saruga entry (2.21.12.19, p. 31) gives villages only; Mabuso Stock typology (2.21.16, pp. 35-36) gives segment inventories (Saruga: no voiced/voiceless stop contrast), nothing on stress or tone.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1970. Languages of the Western Madang District. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, 1271-1292. Pacific Linguistics C-13. Canberra: ANU. hdl:1885/253814
sources.note: Phylum-level typology only ('Notes on the typology of the languages', pp.1279-81: absent phonemes, no number marking, dual forms, possessive classes, suffixing); Saruga occurs only in the classification chart; nothing on stress, accent or tone for any Mabuso language.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Western Madang district, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University, Canberra. 1 v. (346 pp. scan). hdl:1885/130077
sources.note: Survey-wide disclaimer only (p.13, p.22): 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' Saruga entry 2.21.12.19 (p.~47): 'Village: Saruga. Fieldwork will be necessary to ascertain if other villages should be included in the language area. Previously unrecorded.' Sec. 2.21.17 'Typological Features of the Mabuso Stock' gives segment inventories: 'There appears to be no phonemic contrast between voiced and voiceless stops in Amele, Bau, Mawan, Utu, Saruga and Kare'. No word for tone/accent/pitch anywhere in the thesis.

sources.citation: Schebesta, Josef. 1942-45 [publ. 1947]. Ethnographische Miszellen von einer Dienstreise in der Mission von Alexishafen in Neuguinea (mit Anmerkungen von Georg Höltker). Anthropos 37-40: 884-886.
sources.note: no phonology content: the Saruga paragraph (p.885) reads 'Saruga: Dagegen haben die Bögen der Saruga-Leute nur aufgeflochtene Widerlager. Die Lanzen sind aus einem einzigen Stück Holz verfertigt.. Die Tontöpfe werden in Saruga ausschließlich von den Männern hergestellt, und zwar in der sog. Spiralwulsttechnik.' The only linguistic remark in the piece concerns Biramur ('moando-Sprachfamilie'), not Saruga.

sources.citation: Höltker, Georg. 1940-41. Verstreute ethnographische Notizen über Neuguinea (Auszüge aus dem Steyler Missionsboten, u.a. A. Puff 1919/20 'Aus der fernen Südsee', R. Nowak 1926/27 'Missionsbeginn im Sarugabezirk', Br. Antonius 1931/32 'Auf zum Ramu!'). Anthropos 35-36: c. 60-63.
sources.note: no phonology content: ethnographic digest (houses, leeches, 'Saruga hat 12 elende Hütten; keine Häuptlinge; Kochtöpfe, Pfeile, Bogen; 1917 wurde die Missionsstation Naké-Saruga gegründet'); single phrase 'bo nariu' (horses = 'große Schweine') and 'kas la mere = gib mir Tabak' without analysis. Also the source Loukotka 1957 cites as 'Nowak, passim' for Saruga.
